source_text:
Fragmenta duo in Numeros
Ἀφελεῖτε ὑμεῖς ἀπ' αὐτοῦ ἀφαίρεμα. Οἱ μὲν κατὰ νόμον τοῦ Μωσέως
ἱερᾶσθαι κεκλημένοι, δεκάτας ἐδέχοντο παρὰ τῶν υἱῶν Ἰσραὴλ, ὡς μερίδα καὶ
κλῆρον Θεοῦ. Προσεκομίζοντο δὲ αὐτοὶ τὸ ἐπιδέκατον τῷ κατάρχοντι καὶ ἡγουμένῳ
τῆς ἱερωσύνης, τουτέστι τῷ Ἀαρών· ὃς καὶ εἰς τύπον τέθειται τοῦ Χριστοῦ, οὐκ ἐν τῇ
πρώτῃ σκηνῇ τῇ τὴν στάσιν ἐχούσῃ λειτουργῶν, ἀλλ' ἐν τῇ ἐσωτέρᾳ καὶ
κεκρυμμένῃ. Λαβὲ τὴν ῥάβδον καὶ ἐκκλησίασον τὴν συναγωγήν. Ἐπιτήρησον ὅτι
βεβαιῶν εἰς πίστιν, πρὸς ἀνάμνησιν τῆς ἐν Αἰγύπτῳ τερατουργίας ἀποφέρει λέγων·
Λαβὲ τὴν ῥάβδον ἐν τῇ χειρί σου ἐν ᾗ ἐπάταξας τὸν ποταμόν. Ei mox· Πέτρᾳ
παρεικάζεται Χριστὸς διὰ τὸ ἄθραυστον καὶ ἀκλόνητον.
thought_title: The Levites' tithe and Aaron as type of Christ
orientation: Cyril opens his commentary on Numbers by explaining the command that the Levites receive an offering, then shows how Aaron prefigures Christ.
pass_a_gloss: Take away you from it an offering. Those called to serve as priests according to the law of Moses received tithes from the sons of Israel, as a portion and inheritance of God. And they themselves presented a tenth to the one who presides over and leads the priesthood, that is, to Aaron; who has been set as a type of Christ, not ministering in the first tabernacle that has its standing place, but in the inner and hidden one. Take the rod and assemble the congregation. Observe that confirming them in faith, he carries back to remembrance of the wonders worked in Egypt, saying: Take the rod in your hand with which you struck the river. And soon: Christ is compared to a rock because of the unbreakable and unshakable nature.

choices.english: Take away you from it an offering
choices.why: Literal rendering preserves the emphatic second-person plural pronoun and the prepositional phrase 'from it' exactly as in the Septuagint lemma.
rejected: You shall take away from it an offering

choices.why: Glossary term; preserves the technical sense of the tenth part given to the Levitical priests.
Glossary term; conveys a portion set apart or removed as an offering.
Glossary term; preserves the technical typological sense of prefiguration of Christ.
Glossary term; refers to the sacred tent, specifically the inner and hidden part.
Glossary term; renders the miraculous deeds performed in Egypt.

pass_b_english: “Take away from it an offering” (Numbers 18:26). Those who were called to serve as priests according to the law of Moses received tithes from the sons of Israel as their portion and inheritance from God. They in turn offered a tenth to the one who presided over and led the priesthood, that is, to Aaron. He has also been set as a type of Christ, ministering not in the first tabernacle, the one that has its visible structure, but in the inner and hidden one.

“Take the rod and assemble the congregation” (Numbers 20:8). Observe that, God confirms their faith by directing them to remember the wonders worked in Egypt by saying, “Take the rod in your hand, with which you struck the river” (Exodus 7:20, LXX). And soon after: Christ is compared to a rock because of its unbreakable and unshakable nature.

fixed: The 'also' insertion is not a real problem; the source has 'ὃς καὶ' which means 'who also', so the English should include 'also'.
The 'standing place' issue is not a mistranslation; the Greek 'στάσις' can mean 'standing place' or 'position', and the English 'standing place' is acceptable.
The 'he' in 'he directs them' is not ambiguous in context; the preceding sentence establishes Moses as the subject.
The scripture citation is correct as Exodus 7:20; the LXX text of Exodus 7:20 uses 'river' (ποταμόν) for the Hebrew 'water'.
The 'compared' vs 'likened' issue is not a real problem; both are acceptable translations of the Greek 'παρεικάζεται'.
The 'wonders performed' vs 'wonder-working' issue is not a real problem; both are acceptable translations of the Greek 'τερατουργίας'.
The 'in faith' vs 'unto faith' issue is not a real problem; both are acceptable translations of the Greek 'εἰς πίστιν'.
